title: Boron vacancies in bulk h-BN created by high-energy He+ irradiation
authors: P. G. Vilyuzhanina, S. V. Bolshedvorskii, R. Isayev, A. S. Doroshkevich, A. A. Tatarinova, V. V. Soshenko, I. S. Cojocaru, A. M. Kozodaev, S. M. Drofa, A. Chernyavskiy, N. I. Salangin, A. N. Smolyaninov, A. Y. Kuntsevich, A. V. Akimov
abstract: While color centers in diamond and other three-dimensional crystals are nowadays key elements of several types of sensors, color centers in two-dimensional materials are rapidly developing and promise high-tech applications. One of the interesting centers in 2D materials is the negatively charged boron vacancy in hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), which has already shown some potential for magnetometry, but the reliable creation of boron vacancies remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the fabrication of negatively charged boron vacancy color centers in bulk h-BN via implantation of helium ions at ~1 MeV, as confirmed by characteristic photoluminescence and optically detected magnetic resonance. The resonance has a width of 180 MHz and exhibits the expected Zeeman shift of the resonance lines. The depth of the color center along the c-axis of the h-BN crystal was measured and compared with predictions from Stopping and Range of Ions in Matter modeling. The experimental value and the modeled prediction are consistent within the reported uncertainties, as their 1σ intervals overlap, although the experiment shows a greater depth and a wider distribution.
summary: This work reports on the successful creation and detailed characterization of negatively charged boron vacancy color centers in bulk h-BN using high-energy helium ion irradiation. By employing ODMR and PL spectroscopy, the authors confirmed the spin properties of the defect and measured its physical depth. This research advances the use of 2D materials for solid-state quantum memory and sensing applications.
main_problem: The paper focuses on demonstrating the reliable fabrication and characterizing the negatively charged boron vacancy ($	ext{B}_{	ext{V}}^-$) color center in bulk hexagonal boron nitride ($	ext{h-BN}$).
main_result: The authors successfully confirmed the creation of $	ext{B}_{	ext{V}}^-$ centers using characteristic photoluminescence and optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) measurements.
method: The research combines experimental techniques like high-energy $	ext{He}^+$ ion irradiation, PL, and ODMR with theoretical modeling (SRIM) to characterize the defect.
model_or_system: The system is the $	ext{B}_{	ext{V}}^-$ color center in bulk $	ext{h-BN}$. The electronic structure is modeled by a Hamiltonian involving zero-field splitting ($D$) and orthorhombic splitting ($E$), which governs its spin $S=1$ behavior in a magnetic field.
key_observables: Photoluminescence (PL) spectrum (peak at 800–850 nm), Zeeman shift in ODMR resonance lines, and the depth profile of the color center along the c-axis.
important_parameters: Zero-field splitting parameter ($D \approx 3.48 	ext{ GHz}$), orthorhombic splitting ($E \approx 50 	ext{ MHz}$), and the measured resonance width ($180 	ext{ MHz}$).
main_assumptions: The primary discrepancy noted is that the experimental depth of the vacancy is greater than the depth predicted by standard SRIM modeling, suggesting unaccounted physical processes like ion channeling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, the energy level diagram of the $	ext{B}_{	ext{V}}^-$ center, and schematics of the confocal microscope setup used for ODMR measurements.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of problem definition (need for 2D color centers), experimental demonstration (irradiation, PL, ODMR), quantitative analysis (measuring Zeeman shifts and depth), and comparison with theoretical modeling.
why_interesting: The $	ext{B}_{	ext{V}}^-$ center acts as a solid-state spin qubit candidate. The detailed characterization of its spin Hamiltonian parameters ($D, E, \gamma$) and its integration into a robust fabrication protocol are highly relevant for quantum information research.
